title: Gluten-Free Chocolate Orange Cupcakes
shortDescription: Rich gluten-free chocolate cupcakes with fresh orange zest, ready in 43 minutes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These gluten-free chocolate orange cupcakes mix deep cocoa with bright citrus zest. I tested this batch in my home kitchen using a gluten-free flour blend, and the crumb stayed soft and moist.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups gluten-free all-purpose flour blend (with xanthan gum)
1 cup semisweet chocolate chips, melted and cooled
4 oz semisweet chocolate, melted and cooled (for frosting)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the gluten-free flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, beat eggs and sugar until pale, about 2 minutes.
Add oil, buttermilk, orange zest, orange juice, and vanilla. Whisk until smooth.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir gently until just combined.
Fold in the melted chocolate until the batter turns a deep, even brown.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
For frosting, beat softened butter until fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add powdered sugar, melted chocolate, and heavy cream. Beat until smooth and glossy.
Pipe frosting in a tall swirl on each cooled cupcake and top with a pinch of orange zest.
tips: Zest the orange before you juice it. It is much easier that way.
Let the melted chocolate cool for 5 minutes before folding it into the batter, so it does not cook the eggs.
Check your gluten-free flour blend label. Blends without xanthan gum need an extra 1/4 tsp added to the dry mix.
Room temperature eggs and buttermilk blend faster and give a smoother batter.

faq.question: Can I use a different gluten-free flour blend?
faq.answer: Yes, but pick a cup-for-cup blend that already has xanthan gum. Blends without it can make the crumb crumbly.

faq.question: Why does my batter look thin before baking?
faq.answer: This batter is meant to be pourable, thinner than regular flour batter. It thickens as it bakes and still rises well.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy-free too?
faq.answer: Swap the buttermilk for a dairy-free milk with 1 tsp lemon juice, and use dairy-free butter and cream in the frosting.

faq.question: How do I stop the orange flavor from getting lost?
faq.answer: Use fresh zest, not dried, and add it right into the wet mix so the oils release into the batter.

conclusion: These cupcakes prove gluten-free baking can taste rich and full of flavor. The orange zest keeps the chocolate from feeling heavy, and the swirl frosting makes them look bakery ready.
